status: DONE. 47 tests are committed in `07376b4a` and all 47 fail for the stated reason: the validator does not exist yet.
work_completed: Commit `07376b4a` on `w2/W2-51` holds 47 tests in `tests/acceptance/W2-51/` and a README. The README maps each KPI line to its tests and fixes the interface and readings below. Each test builds its own plan tree in `tmp_path`. Contract ids in the trees are fictitious (CAP-91 to CAP-99), and no file in the folder names a real covers id, so the folder can never count as citing a real Contract item.
- **KPI lines and their tests:**
  - Line 1, reading the plan: `test_w2_51_plan_reading.py`, 13 tests. They cover both Contract versions, a ticket with only `external-ref` (`W2-03a`), a WBS row with no ticket and a ticket with no WBS row, and the malformed ids `W2-06ab`, `W2-06A`, `W2-6` neither taken as Wave 2 nor delivering anything.
  - Line 2, the two-way check: `test_w2_51_exit_criterion_7.py`, 10 tests. They cover an item not delivered, an item delivered only by a Wave 1 ticket, a v4.2 lite item not delivered or not cited, an unknown covers id and an unknown capability id, and an id that only Contract 4.2 holds being unknown on a 4.1 tree.
  - Line 3, W2-49's failure KPI: `test_w2_51_cit_p.py`, 7 tests. They cover a 4.1 tree that passes with no CIT-P, a 4.2 tree that passes, an item moved with no CIT-P line, an item moved with no CIT-P file at all, and a CIT-P line with no change in three forms (wave not applied, new item not added, the proposal sitting on a 4.1 tree).
  - Line 4, counts: `test_w2_51_counts.py`, 5 tests.
  - Failure line 1, never the workbench or `docs/source/`: `test_w2_51_outside_inputs.py`, 3 tests.
  - Failure line 2, unreadable inputs: `test_w2_51_unreadable_inputs.py`, 9 tests. The cases are a missing contract, an unparsable contract, a missing WBS, a missing list, a triage that is a folder, a missing `.tickets/`, broken ticket frontmatter, a CIT-P with no read permission, and a root that does not exist.
- **Interface fixed:**
  - Invocation: `python3 docs/plan/tools/validate_w2.py --root <tree>`, run as a subprocess with `HOME` and the working directory both temporary, and `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src`.
  - Output: one line per check on stdout, `<PASS|FAIL|NOT RUN> <name> — <reason>`, where the name is one token and the reason is never empty.
  - Eight named checks: `wave2-tickets`, `contract-items-delivered`, `contract-items-cited-by-tests`, `ticket-contract-ids-exist`, `cit-p-moved-items`, `cit-p-lines-applied`, `list-counts`, `triage-counts`.
  - Checks that would need the workbench or `docs/source/` print `NOT RUN` under names the implementer chooses, with the need named in the reason. At least one such line is required.
  - Exit status: 0 when no check fails (NOT RUN alone does not fail the run), 1 when any check fails. A missing root exits non-zero and passes nothing.
- **Readings of the open input forms** (README §2, R1 to R12, each with its source). The main ones:
  - A Wave 2 ticket: `wbs_id`, or `external-ref` when there is none, matching `^W2-\d{2}[a-z]?$` (DEC-730, `DAEO-rd0g.md`).
  - Delivery: the item's id appears as a token in an entry of the ticket's `closes:`. This includes W2-16's real entry, which YAML cut at its comma (`<id> (lite`).
  - Citation: any file under `tests/acceptance/` holds the id as a whole token.
  - A Contract id a ticket cites: any `CAP-nn` or `CAP-nn.x` token in the ticket file.
  - "Moved to Wave 2": a covers item with `wave: W2` that is not in WBS §1's list "The Contract's N Wave 2 items, by ticket."
  - A CIT-P line: a `- id:` entry with its `wave:` inside a fenced YAML block of any `docs/changes/*-CIT-P.md`. This is W2-49's CIT-P §6.1 form.
  - "No change": the Contract lacks that id, or holds it in another wave.
  - List counts: the `### 3.n <severity> (<n>)` headings against the rows of each table.
  - Triage counts: every cell of the Counts table against the "Every open row" table.
- **Red reason seen:** every test fails with `docs/plan/tools/validate_w2.py does not exist yet: the Wave 2 plan validator is not written (W2-51 not implemented)`.
- **Earlier tests rewritten:** none. **Packages:** none.

discoveries:
- I ran the stand-in read-only over this worktree. The readings hold on the real files: the 17 Wave 2 items are delivered through `closes:`, the list's and the triage's counts agree with their rows, and the WBS baseline paragraph gives all 17 items.
- That run also showed two real plan gaps:
  - The WBS §1 table does not list W2-51 or W2-52, though both have ticket files. `wave2-tickets` will fail on the live tree until the table is updated.
  - 14 of the 17 Wave 2 items are not yet cited by any file under `tests/acceptance/`. This is expected mid-wave, but the real run will show `contract-items-cited-by-tests` as FAIL until the tickets' tests land.
- `validate_s1.py` also reads `governance/project/bootstrap.md` and `.claude/settings.json`. A Wave 2 validator modelled on it should not.
risks:
- The "moved to Wave 2" reading (R7) depends on the wording of the WBS §1 paragraph. If the orchestrator rewrites that paragraph after v4.2 merges (for example "The Contract's 20 Wave 2 items"), the moved items become part of the baseline. Their CIT-P lines are still checked by `cit-p-lines-applied`.
- The fixtures also make each moved item say "lite", so the tests cannot tell R7 apart from a reading based on the "lite" marker.
- The tests require at least one NOT RUN line. If the implementer decides no Wave 2 check needs the workbench or `docs/source/`, that test fails. DEC-744 item 2 presupposes such checks exist, but the reading could be contested.
- The access-time test skips on a file system that does not update access times. On this machine (ext4, relatime) it ran and was checked against the mutants.
- The fixtures keep both readings working (each WBS Closes column matches its ticket's `closes:`, and each citation sits in the delivering ticket's own folder), so the tests cannot tell R3 or R4 from those alternatives.
lessons:
- The guard refuses shell variables in Bash write targets, even inside a scratchpad; write with literal paths. An `rm -rf` of the scratch stand-in was refused at the permission prompt. I did not retry it, and the scratchpad goes when the session ends.
- Never name a real covers id in any file under `tests/acceptance/`: under R4 that counts as a citation. Two comments that did so were found and fixed before the commit.
